primitives.name: Team Size Compensation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The side which opposes the 'varsity—the scrub side, as it is called—should always make up by numbers, in the days of early practice, what it lacks in physique and skill.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'n_s': 'number of substitute players on scrimmage', 'n_v': 'number of varsity players', 'n_t': 'total team size'}
primitives.assumptions: Substitute teams must compensate for physical disparity through numerical advantage during early training phases.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When n_s < n_v - 11, leading to insufficient tactical depth.

layer2.mapping: GSI models player skill variance via Bayesian priors; GSE simulates dynamic lineup adjustments based on n_s/n_v ratios.
layer2.telemetry: Observed deviation from optimal substitution ratio during practice sessions.

primitives.name: Scrimmage Line Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: With the last week or two of practice, only one extra man should be allowed in the line, and two
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'l_e': 'extra men permitted in line', 'b_e': 'extra men allowed behind line'}
primitives.assumptions: Late-stage practice restricts line expansion to maintain tactical cohesion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exceeding l_e = 1 or b_e > 2 causes loss of structured scrimmage integrity.

layer2.mapping: GSI maps scrimmage structure to constraint satisfaction problems; GSE uses this to model final-form team states.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking adherence to line/behind limits per session phase.

primitives.name: Minimum Player Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: The game can be played by still smaller numbers in like fashion; but less than eight on a side breaks up the method materially.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'n_min': 'minimum viable player count per side', 'n_act': 'actual active players per side'}
primitives.assumptions: Below n_min = 8, game mechanics become non-functional due to structural collapse.
primitives.breakdown_regime: n_act < 8 results in invalid tactical configurations.

layer2.mapping: GSI enforces minimum player thresholds via probabilistic game state validation; GSE applies these as hard constraints in simulation.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of games played below n_min threshold.
